en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Eighteenth Chapter
The Discussion on the Intermediate Jhāna:
Is there an intermediate jhāna?
Yes, [it is] affirmed.
Is there an interval between contacts? …pe… Is there an interval between perceptions?
One should not say so …pe….
Is there such a thing as an intermediate dhyāna? Yes.
Is there an intermediate dhyāna between the second dhyāna and the third dhyāna? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there an intermediate meditative absorption (jhānantarika)? Yes.
Is there an intermediate dhyāna between the third dhyāna and the fourth dhyāna?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is there no intermediate dhyāna between the second dhyāna and the third dhyāna?
“Yes.
“If there is no intermediate dhyāna between the second dhyāna and the third dhyāna, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘There is an intermediate dhyāna.’”
Is there no intermediate meditative absorption (jhānantarika) between the third jhāna and the fourth jhāna? Yes.
If there is indeed no intermediate meditative absorption between the third jhāna and the fourth jhāna, then certainly you should not say [that there is].
“There is an intermediate jhāna.
Is there an intermediate jhāna between the first jhāna and the second jhāna? Yes.
Is there an intermediate meditative absorption (jhānantarika) between the second jhāna and the third jhāna?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is there an intermediate meditative absorption between the first jhāna and the second jhāna?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is there, then, an intermediate state of jhāna between the third jhāna and the fourth jhāna?
[The respondent replies: “One should not say so…” and so forth.
Is there no intermediate dhyāna between the second dhyāna and the third dhyāna? Yes.
Is there no intermediate dhyāna between the first dhyāna and the second dhyāna?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there no intermediate dhyāna between the third dhyāna and the fourth dhyāna? Yes.
Is there no "intermediate dhyāna" (jhānantarika) between the first dhyāna and the second dhyāna?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is concentration that is without initial application (avitakka) and consists of sustained application only (vicāramatta) an intermediate dhyāna? One should not say so.
“Yes.
“Then you must not say that concentration accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is ‘the intermediate jhāna’ … [and so on].”
Is concentration that is without initial application but with sustained application "the intermediate jhāna"? Yes.
Is concentration that is without initial application and without sustained application "the intermediate jhāna"?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is concentration accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought not an intermediate dhyāna? Yes.
Is concentration that is without applied thought but with sustained thought not an intermediate dhyāna?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is concentration that is without applied thought and without sustained thought not an intermediate dhyāna? One should not say so.
“Yes,” you say.
“Is concentration that is without applied thought and consists of sustained thought alone not an intermediate jhāna?
You must not say so… [and so on].
Is it the case that when two jhānas are present, there is a concentration consisting of non-thinking and mere sustained thought?
Yes. But when a concentration consisting of non-thinking and mere sustained thought is occurring, has the first jhāna ceased and has the second jhāna arisen? Yes.
“Yes.

“If, when a concentration that is without initial application and with sustained application alone is occurring, the first jhāna has ceased and the second jhāna has arisen, then surely it should not be said:
‘Between two jhānas that have arisen, there is a concentration without initial application and with sustained application alone, which is an interval between jhānas.’”
Is concentration that is without applied thought and consists of sustained thought not an intermediate jhāna?
Yes. Is concentration that is without applied thought and consists of sustained thought the first jhāna? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
Is it the second jhāna …pe… the third jhāna …pe… the fourth jhāna?
It should not be stated thus.
For if that were so, then concentration without applied thought and with sustained thought alone would be the "intermediate jhāna.
Is concentration without applied thought and with sustained thought alone the intermediate jhāna?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “But have not three kinds of concentration been spoken of by the Blessed One:

‘concentration with directed thought and sustained thought,’ ‘concentration without directed thought and with sustained thought only,’ and ‘concentration without directed thought and without sustained thought’?”
“Yes.
“If it is true that three kinds of concentration were spoken of by the Blessed One:
‘with applied thought... [and so on].”
“Concentration without investigation”— surely you should not say,
“Concentration without applied thought and with investigation only is the intermediate jhāna.
The Discussion of the Intermediate Jhāna is finished.
